accuracy.evidence: Every fact in 607 checked against CCSS 1.NBT.5 (find 10 more/10 less mentally, without counting) and NC Y3 ('find 10 or 100 more or less'). All numbers worked: 23→33→43, 46→76, 58→48→38, cross 35/55/44/46 around 45, 10 more than 90 is 100. Parameter ranges keep answers inside 1–100 (a 1–8 for +10, a 2–9 for −10).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips for 1.NBT.5: changing the ones digit (57 for 10 more than 56; Mia's 49), going the wrong way on the hundred square (above vs below), counting on ten single steps instead of using place value, and taking a single cube instead of a ten rod (Take a cube button answers with '1 less').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtenjump is built on the hundred square's row structure (one row = 10) and a cut-out jigsaw cross; flagbundle (bundling 10 ones), flagtenten (10 tens = 100) and flagstair (one more) teach other ideas. Lab gate measured it under 30% shingle overlap with every flag_*.js.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rule before the text states it: dragging the counter shows 10 more lies straight below, adding rods shows the 6 ones never move (46→76), removing rods shows tens fall by 1, and the cross makes them use both directions plus the ±1 sides.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 24 (1 more) for 10 more than 23; 'the ones digit' for adding a ten; 57 (1 less) and 68 (wrong way) for 10 less than 58; 46 (next door) for the box under 45.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Generated questions over 11–89 with three distractor kinds, each with its own message: ±1 ('you changed the ones digit'), wrong direction ('10 less is smaller: one row up'), and ones changed (a±1: 'keep the ones digit'). Sort and cross drops give per-slip feedback too.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and concrete words (tens, ones, box under); validator FK check passes the family kid target 5.0 and adult 10.0. Lab text is one short line per step; age 6–7 terms: tens digit, ones digit, hundred square, place value.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate found no filler phrases; each kid line states a step of the method or an example, adult lines give the standard, the place-value reason, named mistakes and what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light for all 7 steps: hundred square cells ~33 px with 11 px numbers, young-size 56 px buttons, rods/digits readable after enlarging the tens/ones labels; nothing clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin (10 more/1 more/10 less, Add/Take a ten, Pick card then Put in box, Pick tile then Put above/below/left/right); canvas aria-label updates with each message; walk.cjs axe clean in both themes on desktop and phone.

sources: CCSS Math 1.NBT.5: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used
Department for Education, National Curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study, Year 2 number and place value; Year 3 'find 10 or 100 more or less than a given number'
